DILG BAGONG PILIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.gov.ph OPINION NO. MR. HOMER R. JAJALLA Secretary to the Sanggunian Municipality of Mahinog Province of Camiguin Dear Mr. Jajalla: This has reference to your letter dated February 16, 2024, requesting this Department's opinion on the following issues, to wit: 1. What kind of record, i.e., a journal or minutes, shall the Sanggunian or the Secretary to the Sanggunian keep? 2. Are there distinctions between a journal and a minute? and 3. Are there prescribed forms forjoumals and minutes? Ostensibly, the Sangguniang members are divided on whether to record sessions in a journal or through minutes. In reply thereto, we deemed it wise to address the foregoing queries in one discussion, as these are interrelated. Attention is respectfully invited to the pertinent provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code), thus: "Section 52. Sessions. — (e) Each sanggunian shall keep a iournal and record of its proceedings which may be published upon resolution of the sanggunian concerned." Parenthetically, Section 469 (c) of the Code provides: (c) The secretary to the sanggunian shall take charge of the office of the secretary to the sanggunian and shall: (1) Attend meetings of the sanggunian and keep a journal of its proceedings. (6) Record in a book kept for the purpose, all ordinances and resolutions enacted or adopted by the sanggunian, with the dates of passage and publication thereof. Xxx." (Emphasis ours) The aforequoted provisions are instructive and require no further elucidation. As could be clearly gathered therefrom, the Code explicitly mandates the sanggunian to keep a joumal of its proceedings. In the same vein, it expressly mandates the secretary to the "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

sanggunian to keep a journal of the sangguniang proceedings. Along this line, it is worth noting that the Code does not offer a precise definition of what constitutes a "journal" or "minutes," nor are these terms explicitly and strictly defined in statutory language; nevertheless, their meaning and usage are well-established in legislative practice. On that note, the exact form and structure of the journal and minutes are not expressly prescribed in the Code. At any rate, in the sanggunian context, a journal is commonly understood as a comprehensive, exhaustive, and detailed record of all discussions, proceedings, decisions, actions, and other pertinent activities of the sanggunian that transpired during its sessions. On the other hand, minutes are typically concise and provide a recapitulation or abridged version of the sanggunian's proceedings. Unlike journals, which are more detailed and comprehensive, minutes include only the highlights or key discussions of the sanggunian. It is to be noted, however, that while the Code does not explicitly mandate the sanggunian or the secretary to the sanggunian to keep and maintain minutes for recording their sessions or proceedings, nor does it prescribe a specific format for such documents, in practice, keeping and maintaining minutes can streamline and enhance the internal affairs of the sanggunian, thereby optimizing its operational efficiency. Further, the sanggunian, through their internal rules of procedure, may establish and adopt their own format and structure for their journal and minutes to ensure consistency and accuracy. Accordingly, it is ideal and practical for the sanggunian or the secretary to the sanggunian to keep and maintain minutes alongside joumals. To be clear, keeping both journals and minutes are not mutually exclusive; hence, instead of looking at the upkeep of journals and minutes as distinct tasks, the sanggunian and the secretary to the sanggunian should endeavor to maintain both documents as they both serve complementary functions in ensuring the efficacy and efficiency of the sangguniang operations. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, B uthority of the Secretary: AN VIC OR R. LLAMAS de cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUS JVRULLLS-LRALLD/jam DIR. WILHELM M. SUYKO, CESO Regional Director, DILG-X (Northern Mindanao) Masterson Ave., Km. 8, Upper Carmen Cagayan de Oro City Page 2 of 2
